title: Renting vs buying
examples: What is the biggest difference in monthly costs?
How does a mortgage payment compare to rent?
Should I calculate for maintenance when comparing?

explain.say: Today we compare the costs of renting versus buying a home. We will look at the main financial differences.
Renting generally involves predictable monthly payments covering shelter. You do not build equity when you rent your home.

items: Rent is a fixed monthly expense.
It covers your basic shelter needs.
Your payment does not build personal wealth.

explain.say: Buying requires significant upfront costs like a deposit and closing fees. You build equity with every payment you make.
Mortgages are loans used to purchase property, requiring regular principal and interest payments. Understanding interest rates is very important.
A real-life example is comparing a monthly rent payment to a mortgage payment. The mortgage payment must cover more than just the loan.

items: Monthly Payment | Rent Amount | Mortgage + Taxes
Extra Costs | Utilities Only | Utilities + Insurance

explain.say: The most common mistake is only comparing the headline monthly payment. Remember to include property taxes and maintenance costs for buying.

items: They increase the true cost of ownership.

faq.q: How much of my mortgage payment goes to the bank?
faq.a: A portion of your payment goes to paying down the principal loan amount. The rest covers the interest charged by the lender.
asks: Where does my loan money go?

faq.q: Is it always cheaper to buy than to rent?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Initial costs, market fluctuations, and your personal financial goals must be weighed carefully.

faq.q: What is closing costs when buying a home?
faq.a: Closing costs are fees paid at the end of the purchase. These cover things like title insurance and legal fees.
asks: What do I pay when I sign the papers?
Are there extra fees when buying?

faq.q: Does renting help me build wealth?
faq.a: No, renting payments do not contribute to building personal equity or assets. Your money goes to the landlord.
asks: Can I save money by renting?
Does rent count as an investment?

faq.q: What is the difference between a deposit and a down payment?
faq.a: While often used interchangeably, a deposit might be for a rental, whereas a down payment is specifically for the purchase price of the home.
asks: What is the difference between the two upfront payments?

facts: Renting payments do not build personal equity.
Buying requires a significant upfront deposit.
A mortgage payment covers both principal and interest.
Property taxes are a mandatory cost for homeowners.

quiz.say: If you only compare the headline monthly payment, you might forget to include:
quiz.why: Because these are mandatory, recurring costs that increase the true expense of ownership.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it is a large, visible number, but it ignores other essential costs.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the deposit is a one-time cost, not a recurring monthly expense.
wrong.2: While important, utilities are variable and do not represent the full scope of ownership costs.

quiz.say: Which financial activity directly contributes to building personal equity?
quiz.why: Because paying down the principal amount directly increases your ownership stake in the property.

wrong.1: This is common because it is the most visible housing cost, but it does not build equity for you.
wrong.2: While necessary, taxes are payments to the government, not direct equity building for the owner.
wrong.3: These bills cover services used, not the cost of ownership itself.

quiz.say: If a person has a small savings buffer, which initial cost is most relevant to buying?
quiz.why: Because buying requires substantial upfront capital for both the down payment and associated closing paperwork.

wrong.0: Utilities are operational costs, not the primary barrier to entry for buying a home.
wrong.1: This is only one component of the total initial cash needed to close the deal.
wrong.3: This is too small an amount to cover the major upfront requirements of purchasing property.
